chapters.name: Real Numbers
important_points: Every composite number can be uniquely expressed as a product of primes.
If a rational number has a terminating decimal expansion, its denominator in lowest terms has only 2 and/or 5 as prime factors.
Decimal expansion of an irrational number is non-terminating and non-repeating.
formulas: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
diagrams: Standard number line representation of rational and irrational numbers
exam_focus: Finding HCF and LCM using Euclid's algorithm
important_questions: Use Euclid's division lemma to find HCF of two numbers.
Prove that sqrt(2) is irrational.
Find the decimal expansion of a rational number and state whether it is terminating or non-terminating recurring.

chapters.name: Polynomials
topics: Graphs of quadratic and cubic polynomials
important_points: A polynomial of degree n can have at most n zeroes.
For ax^2 + bx + c, sum of zeroes = -b/a and product = c/a.
Zeroes are the x-coordinates where the graph intersects the x-axis.
formulas: For quadratic polynomial ax^2 + bx + c: Sum = -b/a, Product = c/a
If α and β are zeroes, p(x) = k(x - α)(x - β)
diagrams: Graph of a quadratic polynomial showing parabola and x-intercepts
Illustration of zeroes on Cartesian plane
exam_focus: Using relation between zeroes and coefficients
important_questions: Find zeroes of a polynomial and verify the relationship with coefficients.
Divide a polynomial by a linear polynomial and verify the division algorithm.
Draw the graph of a quadratic polynomial and identify zeroes.

chapters.name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
important_points: A pair of linear equations can have no solution, unique solution, or infinitely many solutions.
Graphically, the solution is the intersection point of lines.
formulas: Standard form: a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0
Condition for consistency: a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2 (unique), a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2 (no solution), a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 (infinitely many)
important_questions: Solve a pair of equations using elimination method.
Find whether the system is consistent or inconsistent.
Solve a word problem based on age, cost, or distance.

chapters.name: Quadratic Equations
important_points: A quadratic equation has degree 2.
Discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac determines the nature of roots.
If D > 0, two distinct real roots; D = 0, equal roots; D < 0, no real roots.
diagrams: Parabola for positive and negative roots
Graph of y = ax^2 + bx + c
important_questions: Solve a quadratic equation by factorization.
Find the roots using quadratic formula.
Determine the nature of roots based on discriminant.

chapters.name: Arithmetic Progressions
important_points: Common difference is constant across consecutive terms.
nth term a_n = a + (n-1)d
Sum S_n = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d]
diagrams: Pattern of arithmetic sequence on number line
important_questions: Find the 25th term of an AP.
Find sum of first n terms.
Identify whether a sequence is an AP.

chapters.name: Triangles
important_points: If two triangles are similar, their corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional.
Basic proportionality theorem is useful for solving geometric ratios.
formulas: For similar triangles: AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF
diagrams: Two similar triangles with corresponding sides marked
Right triangle with altitude and theorem application
important_questions: Prove that two triangles are similar.
Use theorem to find unknown sides.
Apply area ratio in similar triangles.

chapters.name: Coordinate Geometry
important_points: Coordinates describe positions on plane.
Distance between two points can be computed using coordinates.
formulas: Section formula: ((m x2 + n x1)/(m+n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m+n))
important_questions: Find the distance between two given points.
Find the midpoint of a segment.
Find the area of triangle formed by three points.

chapters.name: Introduction to Trigonometry
topics: Values of trigonometric ratios for standard angles
important_points: In a right triangle, trigonometric ratios relate angle to side lengths.
sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1 is a fundamental identity.
important_questions: Find sin, cos, tan values for a given angle.
Solve a height-and-distance problem.
Prove a trigonometric identity.

chapters.name: Circles
topics: Number of tangents from a point
important_points: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
Two tangents drawn from an external point are equal in length.
formulas: Radius ⟂ tangent at point of contact
Tangents from external point are equal
diagrams: Two tangents from an external point
important_questions: Prove that radius is perpendicular to tangent.
Find the length of tangent from an external point.
Solve a geometry problem using circle theorems.

chapters.name: Areas Related to Circles
topics: Perimeter and area of a circle
Areas of combinations of plane figures
important_points: Arc length and area of sector are based on angle subtended at the center.
Area of sector = (θ/360) × πr^2
diagrams: Circle with sector and segment shaded
Combined figure of semicircle and rectangle
important_questions: Find area of a sector from radius and angle.
Calculate area of a shaded region made of sectors and rectangles.
Find perimeter of combined shapes.

chapters.name: Surface Areas and Volumes
topics: Cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere, hemisphere
important_points: Surface area of 3D figures measures outside covering. Volume measures space occupied.
Applications include packaging, storage, and construction problems.
formulas: Cuboid: SA = 2(lb + bh + hl), V = lbh
Cone: CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(r+l), V = (1/3)πr^2h
exam_focus: Conversion of one solid to another
important_questions: Find surface area of a cylinder or cone.
Calculate volume of a sphere or hemisphere.
Solve problems with melting and reshaping solids.

chapters.name: Statistics
important_points: Median and mode help summarize data.
For grouped data, class intervals and frequency are essential.
formulas: Mean = sum of values / number of values
Median for grouped data = l + ((n/2 - cf)/f) × h
important_questions: Find mean, median, and mode of grouped data.
Draw an ogive and estimate median.
Interpretation of class intervals.

chapters.name: Probability
important_points: Probability of an event lies between 0 and 1.
P(E) + P(not E) = 1.
formulas: P(E) = Number of favourable outcomes / Total number of outcomes
important_questions: Find probability of head/tail in a coin toss.
Find probability of drawing a card or a ball of a given color.
Solve complementary probability questions.

chapters.name: Light - Reflection and Refraction
important_points: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.
The image formed by a plane mirror is virtual, erect, and laterally inverted.
For lenses, the sign convention follows Cartesian rules.
diagrams: Ray diagram for concave and convex mirrors
Ray diagrams for convex and concave lenses
important_questions: Draw ray diagram for image formation by a concave mirror.
Calculate focal length and magnification using mirror formula.
Explain refraction through a rectangular glass slab.

chapters.name: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
important_points: The eye lens changes shape to focus objects at different distances.
Myopia, hypermetropia, and presbyopia are common defects.
Rainbows are caused by dispersion and internal reflection.
diagrams: Dispersion of white light by prism
important_questions: Define power of accommodation.
Explain myopia and its correction.
Describe the phenomenon of rainbow formation.

chapters.name: Electricity
important_points: Current is the rate of flow of charge.
V = IR is the basic relation of Ohm's law.
important_questions: Calculate resistance in series or parallel combination.
Verify Ohm's law experimentally.
Find electric power consumed by a device.

chapters.name: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
topics: Magnetic field due to current-carrying conductor
important_points: A current-carrying conductor creates a magnetic field around it.
Electric motor converts electrical energy to mechanical energy.
Domestic circuits use fuse for safety.

diagrams: Magnetic field lines around a straight conductor and circular loop
important_questions: Describe magnetic field due to a straight conductor.
Explain the working of an electric motor.
Why is a fuse used in domestic circuits?

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
important_points: Chemical reactions involve rearrangement of atoms.
Balanced equations obey the law of conservation of mass.
formulas: Mass of reactants = mass of products
important_questions: Balance a chemical equation.
Classify a reaction as combination, decomposition, displacement, or double displacement.
Explain corrosion and rancidity with examples.

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
important_points: Acids produce H+ ions in solution; bases produce OH- ions.
pH below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic, and 7 is neutral.
important_questions: Define pH and explain its role in daily life.
Explain the neutralisation process.
List properties of acids and bases.

chapters.name: Metals and Non-metals
topics: Physical properties of metals and non-metals
important_points: Metals are generally malleable, ductile, and good conductors.
Non-metals are brittle and poor conductors of heat and electricity.
formulas: Reactivity series order is used for displacement reactions
important_questions: Compare properties of metals and non-metals.
Explain why iron gets rusted.

chapters.name: Carbon and Its Compounds
important_points: Carbon can form long chains due to catenation.
Organic compounds show homologous series with similar chemical properties.
diagrams: Structural formulas of methane, ethane, ethene
exam_focus: Chemical properties of ethanol and ethanoic acid
important_questions: Explain why carbon forms a large number of compounds.
Write structures and names of first few alkanes.
Differentiate between soaps and detergents.

chapters.name: Life Processes
important_points: Life processes are necessary to maintain life.
Plants and animals use different methods of nutrition and transport.

important_questions: Explain the process of digestion in humans.

important_points: Reproduction ensures continuity of species.
Sexual reproduction introduces variation.
